subject: scale-eating cichlid
title: This Fish Hunts With a Crooked Mouth, and the Crook Keeps Flipping

scenes.text: This fish's mouth is crooked. That's its weapon.
The scale-eating cichlid of Lake Tanganyika lives on scales, ripped off living fish.
It strikes from behind and tears them off the victim's side.
Some grow mouths bent left, which bite the right flank. Others, bent right, bite the left.
Prey learn to guard one side, so the rarer twist lands more bites. About every two and a half years, the majority flips.
A crooked mouth works only as long as it's the rare one.

description:
The scale-eating cichlid Perissodus microlepis of Lake Tanganyika feeds mainly on scales torn from the flanks of living fish, striking from behind.
Its mouth is twisted left or right: left-twisted fish attack the prey's right side, right-twisted fish the left. Michio Hori's field study (Science, 1993) found the rarer form made more successful bites, and the population swung between mostly left and mostly right roughly every 2.5 years.
Are you left or right handed?
first_comment: Lefties attack the right side, righties the left. Would you rather be a lefty or a righty fish?
